Incorporating the April 2023 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) strengthens the statement’s point that tighter credit will weigh on activity. Banks reported broad-based tightening of lending standards and terms across C&I (all firm sizes) and commercial real estate (construction, nonfarm nonresidential, multifamily), as well as most residential and consumer categories (RRE, HELOCs, auto, other consumer). Spreads widened, loan-to-value ratios fell, and debt-service coverage requirements rose. Loan demand was weaker across businesses and households, with credit card demand roughly unchanged. Banks cited a weaker economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, higher funding costs, deposit outflows, liquidity positions, and collateral values as key reasons, and many—along with foreign banks—expect to tighten further.

Implication: Credit transmission is likely to be stronger and more contractionary than the FOMC statement alone suggests, increasing downside risks to growth and hiring even as inflation remains elevated. Net tone stays inflation-focused and data-dependent, but shifts more growth-negative and risk-aware given tighter lending and expected further tightening.
